construct: Distal RTA results from impaired hydrogen-ion secretion by alpha-intercalated cells of the collecting duct, including inherited or acquired defects of apical H+-ATPase-dependent acid secretion. Urine remains inappropriately alkaline despite systemic metabolic acidosis, promoting hypocitraturia and calcium-phosphate nephrolithiasis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hypokalemic normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with persistently alkaline urine and calcium-phosphate stones identifies distal RTA from failure of alpha-intercalated-cell hydrogen-ion secretion.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Proximal RTA can cause hypokalemic NAGMA but distal urine acidification becomes intact at low bicarbonate; type 4 RTA is hyperkalemic; NCC and AQP2 disorders do not produce this acid-base/stone pattern.
